newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil suits not seen as threat to CVRD share sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil suits not seen as threat to CVRD share sale.

text.p: The vice president of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) on Tuesday said he was confident that lawsuits related to the privatization of CVRD would not delay the sale.

The privatization of Companhia Vale do Rio Doce SA, or CVRD, is scheduled to begin on April 29 with the auction of a 40 to 45 percent voting stake in the state-owned mining concern on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange. A minimum price of 3 billion reais ($2.83 billion) has been set.
Borges said similar lawsuits had been filed in connection with the privatization of other companies and the development bank had fought them off successfully.
He said much depended on the judge presiding over the case and not on the legal arguments per se.
Most of the legal challenges focus on the transfer of CVRD's mineral rights to the private sector.
Opponents of the sale say that would violate an article of the Brazilian constitution, which says the country's mineral wealth belongs to the state.
The government argues that the new owners of CVRD would not actually own the mineral rights, but only acquire concessions to exploit them.
